meta.description: Genuine, source-backed threat advisories from Tier 1 Indian Govt Authorities and Tier 3 International Security Agencies with complete HTTPS provenance.

records.title: CERT-In Advisory: Widespread Android Trojan Impersonating Official Utility & Banking Apps
records.summary: CERT-In warns against malicious APK files distributed via WhatsApp, Telegram, and SMS masquerading as utility bill discount updates, PM-Kisan portal updates, or courier tracking tools. Upon installation, the malware requests Accessibility Service permissions to hijack banking OTPs.
records.attackVector: WhatsApp / SMS Phishing -> Malicious APK Sideloading -> Accessibility Hijack
records.technicalDetails: The APK payload utilizes obfuscated Dex code and dynamically requests bind Accessibility Service permissions. Once granted, it captures keystrokes, reads incoming SMS OTPs, and executes automated overlay attacks over popular Indian banking applications.

modusOperandi.step1: Victim receives WhatsApp/SMS claiming electricity connection will be cut or PM-Kisan funds delayed unless bill/KYC is updated.
modusOperandi.step2: Scammer provides link to download a custom APK file.
modusOperandi.step3: App prompts user to grant Accessibility Service and SMS permissions.
modusOperandi.step4: Background service monitors banking app opens and exfiltrates OTPs to external C2 server.

records.impact: Unsanctioned fund transfers via net banking and UPI apps without victim awareness.
records.mitigation: Disable sideloading from unknown sources in Android Settings. Keep Google Play Protect active. Immediately revoke Accessibility permissions for unverified apps.
records.governmentGuidance: Report fraudulent numbers to 1930 Helpline or lodge a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in under the Financial Fraud category within the golden hour.

provenance.who: Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In, MeitY)
provenance.howVerified: Retrieved directly from cert-in.org.in via HTTPS; domain verified against Controlled Source Registry (Tier 1).

records.title: I4C National Advisory: Fake Digital Arrest Extortion & Law Enforcement Impersonation
records.summary: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C, MHA) issues an urgent public advisory regarding structured extortion networks placing video calls via WhatsApp/Skype while impersonating CBI, Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB), Enforcement Directorate (ED), or Cyber Crime Officers.
records.attackVector: IVR / Phone Call -> WhatsApp Video Call -> Fake Court Setup -> Demands for Fund Verification

phishingCallFormats: WhatsApp Video Accounts posing as Police Logos

records.technicalDetails: Scammers setup mock police station studios with uniform-clad impersonators. They issue forged Supreme Court or CBI notices over WhatsApp and force victims into 'Digital Arrest'—demanding continuous camera presence and transfer of money to 'Government Escrow Accounts'.

modusOperandi.step1: Automated call alerts victim that a courier parcel containing illegal narcotics/fake passports was intercepted at customs.
modusOperandi.step2: Call transfers to a 'Police Officer' on WhatsApp video wearing official uniforms in a backdrop mimicking a police station.
modusOperandi.step3: Scammer claims victim's Aadhaar is linked to money laundering and threatens immediate physical arrest unless they remain on video.
modusOperandi.step4: Victim is pressured into liquidating bank deposits into 'RBI Verification Accounts' controlled by money mules.

records.impact: Severe emotional distress and extortion of life savings.
records.mitigation: Remember: No Indian law enforcement agency (Police, CBI, ED, NCB, Customs) conducts video call interrogations or executes 'Digital Arrests'. Never transfer money for police verification.
records.governmentGuidance: Disconnect suspicious video calls immediately. Dial 1930 or report on cybercrime.gov.in under 'Report Cyber Crime'.

provenance.who: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs
provenance.what: National Advisory on Digital Arrest Extortion

records.title: RBI Public Advisory: Fake Customer Care Numbers Posed on Web Search Engines & Map Listings
records.summary: Reserve Bank of India warns citizens against calling customer support phone numbers discovered via public web search results or community-edited map business profiles for banks, e-commerce, or courier companies.
records.attackVector: Search Engine Poisoning -> Fake Support Number -> Remote Access App / AnyDesk Installation

indicators.tactic: Edited Google Maps helpline numbers for private & PSU bank branches

records.technicalDetails: Cybercriminals edit public map listings and publish SEO-optimized fake blog posts containing mobile numbers listed as '24x7 Bank Customer Care'. When victims call for refund help, scammers trick them into installing remote access apps to steal UPI PINs.

modusOperandi.step1: Victim searches online for bank or courier customer helpline number after a failed transaction.
modusOperandi.step2: Victim calls a fake number displayed on a spoofed website or edited map listing.
modusOperandi.step3: Fake executive guides victim to download a 'verification app' (AnyDesk / RustDesk).
modusOperandi.step4: Scammer views victim's phone screen, observes UPI PIN entry, and drains bank balance.

records.impact: Unauthorized financial transfer and device takeover.
records.mitigation: Only obtain customer service details directly from official bank websites printed on passbooks, debit cards, or official mobile apps.
records.governmentGuidance: Report fake listings on search engines and register complaints at 1930 Helpline or National Cyber Crime Portal.

provenance.howVerified: Retrieved from rbi.org.in via HTTPS; domain verified against Controlled Source Registry (Tier 1).

records.title: NPCI Security Advisory: Fraudulent UPI Collect Requests & QR Code Payment Scams
records.summary: National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) issues clarification on UPI safety principles, reiterating that entering a UPI PIN is strictly required ONLY for sending money, never for receiving money.
affectedPlatforms: UPI Apps (BHIM, PhonePe, Google Pay, Paytm)
records.attackVector: OLX / Marketplace Listing -> Scammer Poses as Buyer -> UPI Collect Request / QR Code Scan

phishingTriggers: Scan QR to receive advance payment
Approve UPI Collect Request to receive funds

records.technicalDetails: Fraudsters abuse the 'Request Money' (Collect VPA) feature of UPI or send a QR code claiming it will credit funds. Victims scan the code or enter their 4/6 digit UPI PIN believing funds will be credited, resulting in immediate debit.

modusOperandi.step1: Victim posts an item for sale on online classifieds (OLX, Quikr).
modusOperandi.step2: Fraudster agrees to buy instantly without bargaining and offers advance online payment.
modusOperandi.step3: Fraudster sends a QR code or UPI Collect Request over WhatsApp claiming 'Scan this to receive payment'.
modusOperandi.step4: Victim enters UPI PIN and money is deducted from victim's account.

records.mitigation: Golden Rule: UPI PIN is ONLY needed to TRANSFER money out. Receiving money NEVER requires entering a UPI PIN or scanning a QR code.
records.governmentGuidance: Immediately block the fraudster's VPA in your UPI app and report financial fraud on 1930 Helpline.

provenance.howVerified: Retrieved from npci.org.in via HTTPS; domain verified against Controlled Source Registry (Tier 1).

records.title: CISA Cybersecurity Advisory: Exploitation of Critical Vulnerabilities in Common Edge Gateways
records.summary: CISA and international cyber authorities release joint cybersecurity advisory on active exploitation of unpatched vulnerabilities in perimeter VPNs and edge gateways utilized by enterprise infrastructure.
records.attackVector: Pre-Auth Remote Code Execution -> Edge Appliance Compromise -> Internal Network Lateral Movement
records.technicalDetails: Threat actors leverage memory corruption bugs in web management interfaces of edge devices to achieve remote code execution without authentication, establishing persistent reverse SSH tunnels into internal networks.

modusOperandi.step1: Automated internet scanning for vulnerable edge gateway firmware.
modusOperandi.step2: Execution of HTTP exploit payload against management endpoint.
modusOperandi.step3: Deployment of webshell and persistence scripts.
modusOperandi.step4: Reconnaissance of internal Active Directory environment.

records.impact: Unauthorized network intrusion and risk of ransomware deployment.
records.mitigation: Apply official vendor patches immediately. Restrict management interface access to internal admin networks behind MFA.
records.governmentGuidance: Follow organization patch management policies and monitor network logs for unusual egress traffic.

provenance.who: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (US CISA)
